newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bills trade subdued by high o/nite rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bills trade subdued by high o/nite rates.

text.p: Secondary trading in Philippine treasury bills continued to remain lacklustre on Wednesday as investors were lured away by the central bank's high overnight rates, traders said.
"Buying is just restricted to servicing of clients. No one wants big positions, so there's no demand," one trader said.
Many banks were not even quoting rates for 91-days to one-year but some were very keen to sell the shorter end.
"I saw one offer for two weeks at 16 percent," the trader said.

T-bills quotes from three banks showed one bank had retained at Tuesday's level its bid offer quotes for 91-day bills at 14/13.5 percent but dropped one-year to 15.75/14.75 from the previous 16.25/15.25.
Another bank raised both 91-days as well as one-year. The three months was quoted at 13.875/13.5 from 13.75/13.25 while one-year was raised to 15.50/14.5 from 15.25/14.0.
The average interbank call loan rate remained at 32.1875 percent, with done rates at 36/32.03125 percent.
Volume was lower at 13.01 billion pesos from 19.11 billion. Despite the high rates, the market had 29 lenders out of 42 participating financial institutions.
